messages:
Maria: hey team, running into a weird client-side deadlock when using the JS SDK paginator + retry middleware. paging stops after ~10 pages and we see a spike of 429s. repro below.

Aj: can you paste the minimal repro and logs? is this JS or py? which sdk version?

Maria: JS sdk v1.3.4 (installed from npm last week). minimal usage:

```
const results = [];
for await (const page of client.listItems.paginate({ pageSize: 20 })) {
  results.push(...page.items);
}
```

we have a concurrency limiter at 8 concurrent API calls and retries enabled globally (retry=3, backoff=200ms). logs show many `Retry-After` but the semaphore count doesn't seem to drop, and pagination stalls.

Kevin: hmm. do you have raw request logs? specifically whether retries are queued or if new attempts bypass the limiter

Maria: snippet of logs:

```
[13:02:11] req id=abcd page=4 started
[13:02:11] req id=efgh page=5 started
[13:02:11] resp 429 id=abcd Retry-After=1
[13:02:12] retry attempt=1 id=abcd spawned
[13:02:12] semaphore held=8
[13:02:12] resp 200 id=efgh
[13:02:12] req id=ijkl page=6 started
[13:02:13] semaphore held=8
```

Samir: from that it looks like retries create new request promises that immediately try to acquire the semaphore but if acquire is synchronous the original holder isn't released until the retry path resolves? Could be a leak in the retry wrapper.

Aj: in py sdk we do a `with semaphore:` around the whole request+retry loop so retries wait for the semaphore to be reacquired. JS implementation might `acquire` only for the initial call and then spawn retry timers that also `acquire` but the original never releases because of promise chaining.

Maria: yeah, reproduction: if first attempt gets 429 and the retry backoff is short (200ms), multiple tasks pile up waiting and sem count stays at max because the initial holders never call `release()` until all retries settle.

Kevin: can we confirm if pagination is using a shared queue or per-iterator? if the paginator eagerly prefetches pages it could allocate more concurrency than expected.

Maria: paginator has `prefetch: 2` enabled by default. so it kicks off next pages in background.

Samir: TL;DR root causes:
- prefetch + per-page concurrency cap can oversubscribe when retries re-acquire semaphores incorrectly
- retry wrapper is not properly releasing on early failure path
- default prefetch small but combined with high concurrency produces deadlock-like stalls

Aj: mitigation options:
- short term: disable prefetch (set `prefetch: 0`) or reduce concurrency to 2
- mid term: fix retry wrapper to always release/on finally, and make retries honor the same acquire/release lifecycle
- add queue depth metric and backpressure signal in paginator

Maria: agreed. I'm opening an issue with repro + logs. assigning to @kevin for patch. also adding a unit test that simulates 429+retry to ensure no semaphore leak.

Kevin: taking it. plan:
1) reproduce in CI using mocked 429 responses
2) update retry wrapper to `try { await request } finally { release() }` semantics
3) make prefetch opt-in instead of default
4) publish 1.3.5 as hotfix

Samir: don't forget to test SDK parity: py already uses `with semaphore:` pattern so we'll add a parity test to ensure both SDKs block retries behind the same concurrency guard.

Maria: one more UX note — onboarding docs mention `prefetch` but not how it interacts with retries+concurrency. I'll add a short blurb to quickstart and the pagination README.

Aj: sounds good. @devex-bot please create a GH issue and link the CI job when ready :)

devex-bot: Created issue #1427: "JS SDK paginator + retry semaphore leak causing pagination stalls". CI job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/1427-repro

Maria: thanks :thumbsup: I'll paste the minimal repro link into the issue and put the failing test in the PR.

Kevin: ETA for patch today EOD. if we need to hotfix production customers we can roll 1.3.5.

Samir: also add a telemetry counter for "paginator-prefetch-waiting" so we can detect this pattern in hosted.

Maria: noted. ping me if you want me to attach load traces from the customer.

Aj: great convo. closing loop when PR is merged.

Maria: closing the thread, will update issue with PR link.
